question:
A 59-year-old male presents to clinic with complaints of sexual dysfunction over the past 4 months,
coinciding with increased marital stress following a family death. He maintains normal libido and
morning erections but reports difficulty achieving ejaculation despite being able to attain erections. His
hobbies include regular cycling. His medical history is significant for depression and diabetes,
managed with long-term citalopram and metformin respectively, with no recent medication changes.
Physical examination reveals no abnormalities. What is the most probable cause of his symptoms?
Answer Choices: (A) Autonomic neuropathy due to diabetes (B) Chronic pelvic floor dysfunction (C)
Peripheral arterial disease affecting genital blood flow (D) Medication side effect (E) Psychological
stress (F) Vascular insufficiency due to prolonged cycling (G) Damage to the pudendal nerve (H)
Testosterone deficiency (I) Overuse injury to the perineal region (J) Spinal cord compression affecting
sacral nerves
 A. Psychological stress
B. Autonomic neuropathy due to diabetes
C. Peripheral arterial disease affecting genital blood flow
D. Medication side effect
E. Overuse injury to the perineal region
F. Chronic pelvic floor dysfunction
G. Damage to the pudendal nerve
H. Vascular insufficiency due to prolonged cycling
I. Testosterone deficiency
J. Spinal cord compression affecting sacral nerves
